{
  "root_cause": "The modal's click listener uses event.target.closest to detect the close trigger, causing any click inside the modal (including on checkboxes) to bubble up to the overlay and close the modal.",
  "repair_strategy": "Change the click listener to only close when the clicked element itself has the close-trigger attribute, using hasAttribute instead of closest, so that interacting with inner controls does not inadvertently close the modal.",
  "edits": [
    {
      "path": "lib/src/index.js",
      "sha256": "0db2038c36c8c8c4730018c0ea419249e45923efa8315729f12b4d8da0d5fa2c",
      "before": "    onClick (event) {\n      if (event.target.closest(`[${ this.config.closeTrigger }]`)) {\n        event.preventDefault()\n        event.stopPropagation()\n        this.closeModal(event)\n      }\n    }",
      "after": "    onClick (event) {\n      if (event.target.hasAttribute(this.config.closeTrigger)) {\n        event.preventDefault()\n        event.stopPropagation()\n        this.closeModal(event)\n      }\n    }"
  },
  "expected_accessibility_effect": "Pressing Space on the weekly digest checkbox will toggle its state and keep the preferences dialog open, allowing further interaction.",
  "functional_risks": [
    "Clicking the modal backdrop will still close the dialog as intended.",
    "If any inner element erroneously carries the data-micromodal-close attribute, it will no longer trigger a close (unlikely)."
  ],
  "verification_requirements": [
    "After pressing Space on #weekly, the #prefs-modal must have aria-hidden=\"false\".",
    "The form #prefs must have digest value including \"weekly\".",
    "Focus should remain within the modal (e.g., on #weekly or another inner element) and not return to the trigger button."
  ]
}

We need to analyze the problem.

From environment: we have a test where step 2 fails: pressing Space on the checkbox (#weekly) does not result in expected state: they expect after pressing space, the modal remains open (aria-hidden false) and form data includes weekly checked. However observed shows that after pressing space, the modal closed? Let's look at observed failed steps:

Failed step index 2: Action {"key":"Space","kind":"press"}.

Before: bbox of input #weekly visible etc. After: They list "after" details but actually showing same as button? Wait after block seems incorrectly copied: It says after: bbox height 47 width 230... selector "#open". That suggests after pressing space, focus moved back to button #open? Actually maybe the modal closed and focus returned to trigger button.

Observations: after pressing space, they observed aria-hidden of #prefs-modal is "true"? Actually assertion expects aria-hidden false, observed "true" -> fail. Also form-data digest expected ["weekly"], observed [] -> fail. So pressing space closed the modal and unchecked? Actually checkbox didn't get checked because modal closed before the change? Or maybe the space key triggered closing of modal via micromodal (since space on button with data-micromodal-close?). But the checkbox is not a close trigger. However micromodal's onKeydown handles ESC (27) and TAB (9) only. Not space. So why would space close modal? Possibly because the checkbox is inside a label, and pressing space toggles checkbox but also triggers click on label? Actually clicking label toggles checkbox. Space on checkbox should toggle it. But maybe the modal is closing due to some other reason: maybe the modal's overlay has data-micromodal-close and clicking anywhere on overlay closes modal. If the space key triggers a click event on the overlay? Not likely.

Let's examine the modal HTML: There's a div class="modal__overlay" with tabindex="-1" data-micromodal-close. Clicking on overlay closes modal. But pressing space on checkbox shouldn't cause a click on overlay.

Maybe the issue is that the checkbox is not focusable when modal opens because of micromodal's focus trapping logic? In observed state before step 2, they show focus on #weekly (the checkbox) and it's visible. So focus is inside modal. Good.

When pressing space, the checkbox should toggle. But after, they say after state shows focus back on #open button (the trigger). That suggests modal closed and focus returned to trigger (as micromodal does on close). So pressing space triggered closeModal.

Why would space cause close? Micromodal's onKeydown only handles ESC and TAB. Not space. Unless there is some other listener: maybe the checkbox itself, when space is pressed, triggers a click event on the label? The label wraps the checkbox and text. Clicking label toggles checkbox. But that shouldn't close modal.

But maybe the label is also a button? No.

Wait: Could be that the modal's overlay has data-micromodal-close and also is focusable? When space is pressed, maybe the browser interprets space as activating the currently focused element if it's a button, but if it's a checkbox, space toggles it. However if the checkbox is not actually focusable due to being hidden? But it's visible.

Alternatively, maybe the modal's close button (#modal-close) is receiving the space key because of some focus loop? Not.

Look at observed focusEvents: sequence: from body to #open (trigger), then from #open to #weekly (checkbox), then from #weekly to #open (button). So after space, focus went back to #open. That indicates modal closed and focus restored to trigger.

Thus something caused modal to close on space keydown. Where could that be? Perhaps the modal's overlay has data-micromodal-close and also is capturing keydown events via document listener? Micromodal adds keydown listener on document in addEventListeners (when modal shown). Its onKeydown only handles ESC and TAB. So not space.

But maybe there is another listener elsewhere: maybe the page has some global keydown listener for space that triggers close? Not in given code.

Could be that the space keypress triggers the button's click event (the open button) because it's still in the tab order? Actually after focusing checkbox, pressing space could activate the checkbox, but also bubble up and maybe trigger click on the overlay if the overlay is positioned under? Not.

Let's think about micromodal's focus trap: retainFocus function ensures focus stays within modal when tabbing. It doesn't handle space.

If pressing space causes the checkbox to be checked, but then maybe the form submission? No.

Wait: The observed after state shows the button #open again visible and focus there. The modal likely closed because the overlay got a click event due to the space bar activating the checkbox which is inside a label, and the label maybe has a click that bubbles to overlay? Not.

Another angle: The modal's overlay has data-micromodal-close and also is focusable (tabindex="-1"). When the modal opens, micromodal sets focus to first node that is not a close trigger. In setFocusToFirstNode, they filter out nodes which have attribute closeTrigger (data-micromodal-close). The closeTrigger is defined as option closeTrigger = 'data-micromodal-close'. So they exclude elements with that attribute from initial focus. The overlay has tabindex="-1" and data-micromodal-close, so it's excluded. Good.

Now, when pressing space, maybe the checkbox triggers a click event that bubbles up to the overlay and because overlay has data-micromodal-close, micromodal's click listener (onClick) triggers closeModal. Indeed, micromodal adds click listener on modal (this.modal.addEventListener('click', this.onClick)). onClick checks if event.target.closest(`[${ this.config.closeTrigger }]`) i.e., if the clicked element or its ancestors have the closeTrigger attribute. The overlay has that attribute. If clicking the checkbox results in a click event whose target is the checkbox, but does it bubble up to overlay? Yes, click events bubble up through the DOM. If you click inside the modal, the event target is the checkbox, then it bubbles to its parent label, then to fieldset, form, modal__container, modal__overlay, etc. Since the overlay has data-micromodal-close attribute, the event.target.closest('[data-micromodal-close]') will match the overlay, causing onClick to call closeModal(event). That would close modal on any click inside modal! That explains behavior: clicking the checkbox (via mouse or space) triggers a click event that bubbles to overlay and closes modal. Indeed, many modal implementations prevent this by stopping propagation or checking that the target is the overlay itself, not any child. Here they just check closest, causing any click inside to close.

Thus the bug: clicking inside modal (including checkbox) closes modal because overlay has data-micromodal-close and click listener treats any descendant as close trigger.

Fix: modify onClick to only close if the target is the overlay itself (or has the closeTrigger attribute AND is the overlay?), typical pattern: close only when clicking on the backdrop, not on modal content. Usually they check if event.target has the closeTrigger attribute (i.e., the overlay) and not its children. Since overlay has tabindex="-1" and data-micromodal-close, we can change condition to event.target.hasAttribute(this.config.closeTrigger) instead of closest. Or we can check that event.target matches the overlay (i.e., event.target === this.modal.querySelector('.modal__overlay')). Simpler: change to if (event.target.hasAttribute(this.config.closeTrigger)).

Let's verify: overlay has attribute data-micromodal-close. The checkbox does not. So clicking checkbox will not satisfy hasAttribute, thus not close. Clicking overlay directly will close.

Thus edit in lib/src/index.js, in onClick method.

Repair strategy: Change the click handler to only close when the clicked element itself has the close-trigger attribute, preventing accidental closure from inner elements.
